Plot the principal coordinates of phylogenetic structure

Source: R/pcps.R
plot.mc_pcps.Rd

Draws the sites on two principal coordinates of pcps_test(), coloured by a predictor, with the species as arrows from the correlation of their column of the matrix P with the axes, as in the biplot of the package PCPS (Debastiani & Duarte 2014). With clades, the species are drawn as stars coloured by clade, each clade with its outline and name, as in Fig. 1 of Debastiani & Duarte (2014), which shows which lineages go with which sites.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mc_pcps'
plot(
  x,
  axes = c(1, 2),
  env = 1,
  species = TRUE,
  species_labels = TRUE,
  clades = NULL,
  palette = "viridis",
  point_size = 2.5,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

Result of pcps_test().

axes

The two principal coordinates to draw.

env

Predictor that colours the sites: a column number or name of the predictors given to pcps_test(), or NULL for no colour.

species

Draw the species as arrows.

species_labels

Write the names of the species at the arrows or stars.

clades

Optional grouping of the species into clades: a single number k, which cuts the tree into its k deepest clades by splitting, one at a time, the clade whose crown is nearest the root; or a vector of clade names named by species, such as families, in which species left out are drawn in grey without a clade. Each clade with at least three species gets its convex hull.

palette

Name of a palette of grDevices::hcl.colors() for the predictor.

point_size

Size of the site points.

...

Not used.

Value

A ggplot object.

References

Debastiani, V. J., & Duarte, L. D. S. (2014). PCPS – an R-package for exploring phylogenetic eigenvectors across metacommunities. Frontiers of Biogeography, 6. doi:10.21425/F5FBG22943

See also

pcps_test().

Other the whole tree: pcc_test(), pcps_test(), phylo_beta(), phylo_beta_test(), phylo_eigenvectors(), plot_phylo_beta()

Examples

set.seed(1)
tree <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(12)
traits <- species_traits(tree, lambda = 1, optima_range = c(0, 100), rmax_range = c(0, 30))
env <- seq(0, 100, length.out = 36)
comm <- simulate_static(traits, env, incidence = TRUE)$abundance
plot(pcps_test(comm, tree, env, n_perm = 19))
